name: Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome type 2
aliases: Müllerian agenesis with renal and skeletal anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and imaging diagnostic criteria for MRKH syndrome type 2

criteria.description: Congenital absence or hypoplasia of the uterus and upper two-thirds of the vagina
Presence of renal malformations such as unilateral renal agenesis, ectopic kidney, or horseshoe kidney
Associated vertebral anomalies including scoliosis, fused vertebrae, or rib abnormalities
Normal development of secondary sexual characteristics and normal external genitalia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital absence or hypoplasia of uterus and upper vagina plus at least one associated renal or skeletal anomaly
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by clinical examination, imaging studies (MRI/ultrasound), and karyotyping.

laboratory: Normal female hormone profile (FSH, LH, estrogen)
imaging: MRI or ultrasound showing absent or hypoplastic uterus and upper vagina
Renal ultrasound or MRI revealing renal agenesis or ectopia
other: Normal secondary sexual characteristics on physical examination

distinguishingFeatures: Female external genitalia with absent or rudimentary Müllerian structures
Presence of uterus and normal ovaries
Obstructive vaginal anomaly rather than agenesis
Menstrual flow obstruction with cyclic pelvic pain

redFlags: Primary amenorrhea with absent uterus on imaging
Vertebral anomalies or scoliosis in adolescent female with amenorrhea
references: Herlin MK, Björnsdóttir TS, Rasmussen M, et al. Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser (MRKH) syndrome: a comprehensive update. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2020;15(1):214.
Oppelt P, Renner SP, Kellermann A, et al. Clinical aspects of Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome: recommendations for clinical diagnosis and staging. Hum Reprod. 2006;21(3):792-7.
Morcel K, Camborieux L, Guerrier D. Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser (MRKH) syndrome. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2007;2:13.
